setup: Sit tall, back and shoulders against the pad
Fasten the thigh pad or belt if there is one
Grip the handles, elbows bent to about 90°
execution: Push the handles down until your arms are straight
Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides
Let the handles rise slowly to the start
faults: Don't shrug your shoulders up at the top
Don't lean far forward to push

notes: Let the handles come up only as far as your shoulders feel comfortable; a light stretch is enough.
This is a weight-stack machine: the number is load you push, not help. A larger number is harder, unlike the assisted dip.
Machines differ. Read the label for seat and handle settings before you load it.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Seated upright, back on the pad. Hands on the handles beside the lower chest, elbows bent about 90° and pointing back, shoulders down.

keyPositions.label: Bottom
keyPositions.describe: Arms straight, handles pushed down beside the hips. Elbows close to the sides; torso upright.

ikHints: Back and hips fixed on the seat and pad
Hands fixed to the handles, which travel down beside the body
emphasise: Elbows stay tucked close to the body
Full arm straightening at the bottom
